name: Nāthamuni
summary: First ācārya of the Śrīvaiṣṇava lineage (after Nammāḻvār), of Vīranārāyaṇapuram (Kāṭṭumannārkōyil). The tradition says he recovered and arranged the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham, set its hymns to music for temple recitation, and taught yoga; his works on logic and yoga are lost.

tradition.text: 824–924 CE in one commonly cited traditional reckoning; hagiographies give an extremely long life

realization_account.text: Hearing ten verses of the Tiruvāymoḻi ending 'these ten out of a thousand', he sought the rest at Kurukūr, recited Madhurakavi's Kaṇṇinuṇ Ciṟuttāmpu twelve thousand times in yogic absorption, and received from Nammāḻvār in vision the whole four thousand hymns and their meaning.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Uyyakkoṇḍār
summary: Disciple of Nāthamuni and teacher of Maṇakkāl Nambi; the tradition says he preferred the Lord's service to learning yoga.

name: Kurukai Kāvalappaṉ
summary: Disciple of Nāthamuni to whom, the tradition says, the teaching of yoga (yogarahasya) was entrusted; Yāmuna was directed to him but arrived after his death.

name: Maṇakkāl Nambi
summary: Disciple of Uyyakkoṇḍār who, the tradition says, drew Yāmuna back from kingship to the teaching, by bringing him greens daily until admitted, and then leading him to Raṅganātha.

name: Yāmunācārya
summary: Grandson of Nāthamuni and grand-teacher of Rāmānuja; author of the Siddhitraya, Āgamaprāmāṇya, Gītārthasaṅgraha, Stotraratna and Catuḥślokī, who laid the philosophical foundation of Viśiṣṭādvaita and defended the Pāñcarātra.

realization_account.text: As a boy he defeated the court scholar and won half a kingdom, hence 'Āḷavantār' ('he who came to rule'); Maṇakkāl Nambi led him to renounce it. At his death three fingers of his hand stayed folded, for three unfulfilled wishes, and unfolded when Rāmānuja vowed to fulfil them.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Periya Nambi
summary: Disciple of Yāmuna who gave Rāmānuja the five sacraments (pañcasaṃskāra) at Madhurāntakam; the tradition says he was blinded and died under the Cōḻa persecution.

name: Tirukkōṭṭiyūr Nambi
summary: Disciple of Yāmuna who, after making Rāmānuja come to him eighteen times, taught him the secret meaning of the tirumantra and the carama-śloka.

name: Periya Tirumalai Nambi
summary: Disciple of Yāmuna and maternal uncle of Rāmānuja, who taught him the Rāmāyaṇa at Tirupati and brought Govinda (Embār) back to Vaiṣṇavism.

name: Tirumālai Āṇḍāṉ
summary: Disciple of Yāmuna who taught Rāmānuja the meaning of the Tiruvāymoḻi.

name: Tiruvaraṅga Perumāḷ Araiyar
summary: Son (or kinsman) of Yāmuna and temple singer (araiyar) of Śrīraṅgam, one of Rāmānuja's five teachers.

name: Tirukkacci Nambi
summary: Non-brahmin devotee who served Varadarāja at Kāñcī by fanning him; the tradition says the Lord spoke through him the six sayings that settled Rāmānuja's doubts.

realization_account.text: Varadarāja conversed with him directly and answered Rāmānuja's questions through him with six sayings.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Yādavaprakāśa
summary: Kāñcī teacher of bhedābheda Vedānta under whom Rāmānuja first studied; the tradition says they disagreed over Upaniṣadic readings and that he later became Rāmānuja's disciple as the renouncer Govinda Jīyar. (U16 owns his entry; this is U14's contribution.)

name: Rāmānuja
summary: The principal systematizer of Viśiṣṭādvaita: born at Śrīperumbūdūr, he renounced at Kāñcī, led the Śrīraṅgam temple and community, spent years at Melkote during the Cōḻa persecution, and wrote nine works — the Śrībhāṣya, Vedārthasaṅgraha, Vedāntasāra, Vedāntadīpa, Gītābhāṣya, the three Gadyas and the Nityagrantha.

scholarly.text: 11th–12th c. CE; some scholars doubt the 120-year span and propose c. 1077–1157

realization_account.text: Varadarāja answered his doubts through Tirukkacci Nambi; Tirukkōṭṭiyūr Nambi gave him the secret mantra after eighteen visits, and he proclaimed its meaning to all from the temple tower, accepting hell for himself if others could be saved; he surrendered to Śrī and Raṅganātha on Paṅguni Uttiram, and the Lord's reply is recorded in the Śaraṇāgati Gadya. The Śrīvaiṣṇava tradition regards him as an incarnation of Ādiśeṣa (and Lakṣmaṇa).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Kūreśa
summary: Rāmānuja's foremost disciple and scribe, the father of Parāśara Bhaṭṭar and author of the Pañcastava. The tradition says he memorized the Bodhāyana Vṛtti in Kashmir for Rāmānuja and was blinded by a Cōḻa king for refusing to affirm Śiva's supremacy.

name: Mudaliyāṇḍāṉ
summary: Nephew of Rāmānuja, called his 'triple staff' (tridaṇḍa), entrusted with the administration of the Śrīraṅgam temple.

name: Embār
summary: Rāmānuja's cousin Govinda, once a Śaiva at Kāḷahasti, brought back by Periya Tirumalai Nambi; Rāmānuja's successor at Śrīraṅgam and teacher of Parāśara Bhaṭṭar, in the line the Teṅkalai follow.

name: Kiḍāmbi Āccāṉ
summary: Disciple of Rāmānuja who, the tradition says, cooked for him when attempts were made to poison his food; ancestor of the Kiḍāmbi family of teachers in Deśika's line.

name: Tirukkurukaippirāṉ Piḷḷāṉ
summary: Disciple (and adopted son, in tradition) of Rāmānuja who, at his direction, wrote the first commentary on the Tiruvāymoḻi, the Ārāyirappaṭi ('Six Thousand'); a link in the teacher-line the Vaṭakalai follow.

name: Anantāḻvāṉ
summary: Disciple of Rāmānuja sent to Tirumala to maintain a flower garden for Veṅkaṭeśvara.

name: Aruḷāḷa Perumāḷ Emperumāṉār
summary: Formerly the Advaita renouncer Yajñamūrti who, the tradition says, debated Rāmānuja for eighteen days, conceded, and became his disciple; author of the Tamil Jñānasāram and Prameyasāram.

name: Tiruvaraṅgattu Amudaṉār
summary: Śrīraṅgam temple functionary who became Rāmānuja's devotee through Kūreśa and composed the Irāmāṉuca Nūṟṟantāti.

name: Piḷḷai Uṟaṅgāvilli Dāsar
summary: Wrestler of Uṟaiyūr whom, the tradition says, Rāmānuja turned from infatuation with his wife's eyes to the eyes of Raṅganātha; an exemplar of devotion regardless of birth.

name: Viṣṇucitta (Engaḷāḻvāṉ)
summary: Disciple of Rāmānuja and Piḷḷāṉ, author of the Viṣṇucittīya on the Viṣṇu Purāṇa, and teacher of Naḍādūr Ammāḷ in the line the Vaṭakalai follow. (Not to be confused with Periyāḻvār, also called Viṣṇucitta.)

name: Parāśara Bhaṭṭar
summary: Son of Kūreśa, named by Rāmānuja in fulfilment of Yāmuna's wish; successor at Śrīraṅgam after Embār; author of the Śrīraṅgarājastava, Śrīguṇaratnakośa, Bhagavadguṇadarpaṇa and Aṣṭaślokī; the tradition says he won over the Advaitin Mādhava (Nañjīyar).

name: Nañjīyar
summary: Formerly the Advaitin Vedānti Mādhava, converted by Parāśara Bhaṭṭar; renouncer and author of the Oṉpatiṉāyirappaṭi ('Nine Thousand') on the Tiruvāymoḻi; teacher of Nampiḷḷai.

name: Nampiḷḷai
summary: Nampūr Varadarājar, disciple of Nañjīyar, whose lectures on the Tiruvāymoḻi at Śrīraṅgam drew great crowds and were recorded as the Īṭu; called Lokācārya, a title passed to Piḷḷai Lokācārya.

name: Vaṭakku Tiruvīti Piḷḷai
summary: Disciple of Nampiḷḷai who wrote down his teacher's lectures as the Īṭu Muppattāṟāyirappaṭi; father of Piḷḷai Lokācārya and Aḻagiya Maṇavāḷa Perumāḷ Nāyaṉār.

name: Periyavāccāṉ Piḷḷai
summary: Disciple of Nampiḷḷai, called the 'emperor of commentators' (vyākhyāna-cakravarti), who wrote Maṇipravāḷa commentaries on nearly the whole Divya Prabandham, including the Irupattunālāyirappaṭi on the Tiruvāymoḻi.

name: Piḷḷai Lokācārya
summary: Eldest son of Vaṭakku Tiruvīti Piḷḷai, named after Nampiḷḷai (Lokācārya); a lifelong celibate who wrote the eighteen rahasya works in Maṇipravāḷa, above all the Śrīvacanabhūṣaṇam, Mumukṣuppaṭi, Tattvatrayam and Arthapañcakam; the Teṅkalai regard him as their doctrinal source.

tradition.text: 1205–1311 CE in commonly given Teṅkalai dates; the tradition places his death at Jyotiṣkuḍi while escorting Raṅganātha's processional image away from the sack of Śrīraṅgam (an event usually dated 1323 — not reconciled here)

realization_account.text: The Teṅkalai tradition holds that Raṅganātha himself, in the form of a teacher, instructed him, and that he taught the secret doctrine openly out of compassion.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Aḻagiya Maṇavāḷa Perumāḷ Nāyaṉār
summary: Younger brother of Piḷḷai Lokācārya, author of the Ācārya Hṛdayam, which presents Nammāḻvār's Tiruvāymoḻi as the Tamil Veda.

name: Kūrakulottama Dāsar
summary: Disciple of Piḷḷai Lokācārya who, the tradition says, preserved and passed on his teacher's doctrine to Tiruvāymoḻi Piḷḷai.

name: Tiruvāymoḻi Piḷḷai
summary: Teacher of Maṇavāḷa Māmuni, who restored the worship at Āḻvār Tirunagari and handed on the Īṭu and Piḷḷai Lokācārya's works.

name: Maṇavāḷa Māmuni
summary: The last of the great Teṅkalai teachers: disciple of Tiruvāymoḻi Piḷḷai, commentator on Piḷḷai Lokācārya's works and the Ācārya Hṛdayam, author of the Upadēśa Ratnamālai and Yatirājaviṃśati, and founder of the eight 'elephants' (aṣṭadiggaja) among his disciples; the Teṅkalai regard him as Rāmānuja returned.

realization_account.text: After he expounded the Īṭu for a year before Raṅganātha at Śrīraṅgam (1432 in the tradition's reckoning), the Lord appeared as a child and recited the verse 'śrīśaileśa-dayāpātram', taking him as his own teacher.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Poṉṉaḍikkāl Jīyar
summary: Foremost disciple of Maṇavāḷa Māmuni, first head of the Vānamāmalai (Nāṅguneri) maṭha.

name: Prativādi Bhayaṅkaram Aṇṇaṉ
summary: Disciple of Maṇavāḷa Māmuni, one of his eight chief disciples, to whom the Veṅkaṭeśa Suprabhātam is attributed.

name: Piḷḷai Lōkam Jīyar
summary: Teṅkalai author of the Yatīndrapravaṇa Prabhāvam, the life of Maṇavāḷa Māmuni, and of commentaries on the rahasya works.

name: Vādikesari Aḻagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar
summary: Teṅkalai commentator credited with the Paṉṉīrāyirappaṭi ('Twelve Thousand') on the Tiruvāymoḻi.

name: Piṉpaḻagiya Perumāḷ Jīyar
summary: Śrīvaiṣṇava teacher to whom the Ārāyirappaṭi Guruparamparāprabhāvam, the chief hagiography of the Āḻvārs and ācāryas, is attributed.

name: Naḍādūr Ammāḷ
summary: Vātsya Varadaguru, celebrated expounder of the Śrībhāṣya at Kāñcī, whose lectures Sudarśana Sūri recorded in the Śrutaprakāśikā; disciple of Engaḷāḻvāṉ and teacher of Ātreya Rāmānuja.

name: Sudarśana Sūri
summary: Author of the Śrutaprakāśikā on the Śrībhāṣya; the tradition says he perished when Śrīraṅgam was sacked and that Vedānta Deśika saved his manuscript and his sons.

tradition.text: died in the sack of Śrīraṅgam (c. 1323)

name: Ātreya Rāmānuja
summary: Kiḍāmbi Appuḷḷār, maternal uncle and teacher of Vedānta Deśika, disciple of Naḍādūr Ammāḷ; the Nyāyakuliśa is attributed to him.

name: Vedānta Deśika
summary: Veṅkaṭanātha of Tūppul near Kāñcī, poet, logician and theologian; the Vaṭakalai regard him as their doctrinal source. He wrote over a hundred works in Sanskrit, Maṇipravāḷa and Tamil — the Rahasyatrayasāra, Tattvamuktākalāpa, Śatadūṣaṇī, Nyāyasiddhāñjana, Nyāyapariśuddhi, Seśvaramīmāṃsā, Pādukāsahasra, Saṅkalpasūryodaya and many hymns — and lived through the sack of Śrīraṅgam.

realization_account.text: The tradition holds him an incarnation of the bell of Veṅkaṭeśvara; the titles Vedāntācārya and Sarvatantrasvatantra were conferred on him by Raṅganātha and Raṅganāyakī; Hayagrīva, whose mantra he received from Garuḍa, granted him knowledge; he declined royal patronage.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Kumāra Varadācārya
summary: Son and disciple of Vedānta Deśika (Nayinārācārya), author of the Adhikaraṇacintāmaṇi and continuer of his father's line.

name: Brahmatantra Svatantra Jīyar
summary: Disciple of Vedānta Deśika and first head of the Parakāla maṭha (later at Mysore) in the Vaṭakalai line.

name: Ādivaṇ Śaṭhakopa Jīyar
summary: Founder of the Ahobila maṭha of the Vaṭakalai (traditionally 1398), who, the tradition says, received his renunciation from Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha of Ahobilam himself.

tradition.text: founded the Ahobila maṭha in 1398 CE

name: Meghanādāri Sūri
summary: Viśiṣṭādvaita logician before Deśika, author of the Nayadyumaṇi.

name: Doḍḍayācārya
summary: Mahācārya of Ghaṭikāśatam, a Vaṭakalai polemicist who continued Deśika's attack on Advaita in the Caṇḍamāruta; the tradition sets him against Appayya Dīkṣita.

name: Raṅgarāmānuja Muni
summary: Viśiṣṭādvaita commentator on the principal Upaniṣads (the Prakāśikās) and on the Śrībhāṣya.

name: Śrīnivāsadāsa
summary: Author of the Yatīndramatadīpikā, the standard short manual of Viśiṣṭādvaita doctrine.

name: Garuḍavāhana Paṇḍita
summary: Author, by tradition a contemporary of Rāmānuja, of the Sanskrit Divyasūricaritam on the lives of the Āḻvārs and Rāmānuja.

name: Anantārya
summary: Author of the Sanskrit hagiography Prapannāmṛtam (Anantācārya; distinct from Prativādi Bhayaṅkaram Aṇṇaṉ).

name: Nammāḻvār
summary: (U25 owns.) For Viśiṣṭādvaita: the 'first head of the clan' (kulapati) of the Śrīvaiṣṇavas, from whom Nāthamuni received the Prabandham; his Tiruvāymoḻi is the 'Tamil Upaniṣad' (Dramiḍopaniṣad) expounded by the ācāryas, and Deśika's Pādukāsahasra identifies him with the Lord's sandals.

name: Uttamūr Vīrarāghavācārya
summary: 20th-century Vaṭakalai scholar and editor-commentator of Viśiṣṭādvaita works (post-1800; recorded as recent).
